---
title: "beam"
subtitle: "Benchmark Evaluation and Metrics"
---

beam is a metric formalization layer for method comparisons and benchmarks in bioinformatics. It records each performance metric in a [metric card](docs/explanations/cards-and-pipeline.qmd) with [measurement-theory](docs/explanations/measurement-theory.md) grounded metadata, ranks methods with [multi-criteria decision analysis](docs/explanations/aggregation-methods.md), and decomposes [method-dataset heterogeneity](docs/explanations/method-by-dataset-heterogeneity.md).

The metric cards are mapped to STATO, UO, OBI and HuggingFace evaluate where available. The OWL is available at [docs/beam.owl.ttl](docs/beam.owl.ttl) and regenerated from the cards on each release.

## Where to start

- [Quick start](docs/tutorials/quickstart.md). From a CSV to a ranking and an HTML report.
- [How to run from beam.yaml](docs/how-to/run-from-beam-yaml.md). The declarative beam specification.
- [How to use beam from R](docs/how-to/use-beam-from-r.md). The R interface (reticulate-backed; same metric cards and pipeline).
- [Cards and pipeline](docs/explanations/cards-and-pipeline.qmd). What a metric card encodes and how it is processed.
- [Comparing methods across datasets](docs/explanations/critical-difference.md). Diagnostics on method-dataset performance variability.

## Worked vignettes

- [Duo 2018 clustering](examples/duo2018/duo2018.qmd): scRNA-seq clustering with 14 methods on 12 datasets.
- [Simulated scenarios](examples/scenarios/scenarios.qmd): consistency checks against documented ground truth.
- [Transportation modes](examples/transportation/transportation.qmd): cross-domain example with partial coverage.
- [M4 forecasting](examples/m4/m4.qmd): 25 methods on six frequency bands.
- [OpenProblems batch integration](examples/openproblems/openproblems.qmd): MCDA contrasted with the platform's own mean-of-scores rule, plus a Bradley-Terry tree on 50 spatial datasets.
- [Cross-benchmark meta-analysis](examples/cross_benchmark/cross_benchmark.qmd): consistency across independently published scRNA-seq integration benchmarks.
- [LLM cell type annotation](examples/cell_type_annotation/cell_type_annotation.qmd): GPT-4 and GPT-3.5, GPTCelltype etc versus classical annotation methods.

We also provide the standard reports for some of these comparisons.

- [Duo 2018 clustering](docs/reports/duo2018.html)
- [M4 forecasting](docs/reports/m4.html)
- [OpenProblems batch integration](docs/reports/openproblems_batch_integration.html)
- [LLM cell type annotation](docs/reports/gptcelltype.html)
